title: The dynamics of lysozyme from bacteriophage lambda in solution probed by NMR and MD simulations.
experiment: 15N T1, T2 (CPMG 2tau_cp = 1 ms) and {1H}15N heteronuclear NOE relaxation at 500.10 and 750.04 MHz with Lipari-Szabo model-free analysis
other_conditions: ~0.5 mM protein; 128 of 158 residues analysed; tumbling: tau_R = 10.8 ns (500 MHz) and 11.3 ns (750 MHz), axially symmetric diffusion tensor D||/Dperp = 1.278 (fitted on 85 residues); Lipari-Szabo model selection across 128 residues: model 1 (S2, 86 residues), model 2 (S2 + Rex, 12 residues), model 3 (S2 + tau_e, 6 residues), model 4 (S2 + Rex + tau_e, 6 residues), model 5 (S2f + S2s + tau_s, 13 residues), model 6 (S2f + S2s + tau_s + Rex, 5 residues); 仅图示: per-residue S2, {1H}15N NOE, T1/T2, and the full identity of all 22 low-S2 (< 0.85) and 23 Rex residues are shown only in Figure 2
timescale: Rex < 1.0 s-1 or Rex > 1.0 s-1 at 500 MHz across 23 residues, scaled by 2.25 at 750 MHz (per-residue Lipari-Szabo model-free fit, models 2, 4, and 6)
alt_state_structure: 1AM7: open form (molecules A and C) and closed form (molecule B) in apo X-ray crystal structure (Introduction, p. 1780; Fig. 1); 3D3D: closed form in complex with hexa-N-acetylchitohexaose (Introduction, p. 1780; Results and Discussion, p. 1785)
author_claim: Lower lip (residues 51-60) and upper lip (residues 128-141 / 124-140) surrounding the active-site cleft exhibit both reduced {1H}15N NOE and S2 order parameters (< 0.85) indicating picosecond mobility and significant Rex contributions to T2 indicating microsecond-to-millisecond conformational exchange.
anchor: in the lower and upper lip regions indicating that these residues undergo motions on both fast picosecond and slower microsecond
locator: Results and Discussion, 15N relaxation measurements, p. 1781-1782 and Fig. 2 (仅图示 for full per-residue values); Fig. 5 caption, p. 1784; conditions: Experimental Section, 15N NMR relaxation experiments, p. 1786-1787
caveat_note: The 15N T1, T2 and {1H}15N NOE datasets at 500 and 750 MHz are explicitly deposited in BMRB 19127 (p. 1786); BMRB 19127 card lists 293 K (= 20 °C; pdftotext rendered °C as '8C' in paper.txt), pH 5.45, 500/750 MHz, 95% H2O/5% D2O, though the BMRB card sample component string shows placeholder 'natural abundance 0 mM' whereas the paper reports ~0.5 mM 15N-labelled protein. Slight spectrometer temperature differences between 500 and 750 MHz gave tau_R = 10.8 vs 11.3 ns and were corrected with field-specific scaling factors. Exact numerical per-residue S2, Rex, tau_e, and tau_s values are not tabulated in text (Fig. 2A only classifies the 23 Rex residues as < 1.0 s-1 or > 1.0 s-1 at 500 MHz). Note internal text discrepancy on crystal helix alpha6 end residue: p. 1780-1781 gives 135-148 (open) and 139-148 (closed), whereas p. 1785 gives 135-149 and 139-149.

title: The dynamics of lysozyme from bacteriophage lambda in solution probed by NMR and MD simulations.
experiment: 3JHNHa scalar coupling constants (2D HMQC-J at 750 MHz), 3D 15N-edited NOESY-HSQC (750 MHz, 150 ms mixing time), and 1H/13C/15N chemical shift comparison (SHIFTX2 and TALOS+)
other_conditions: 104 residues measured for 3JHNHa (deposited in BMRB 19127): L52 = 6.2 Hz, K58 = 9.4 Hz, K60 = 8.6 Hz in lower lip; H137 = 6.1 Hz, K138 = 5.4 Hz, S141 = 5.9 Hz in upper lip (< 5 Hz only for 144-148); long-range NOEs observed between L55 HN, N56 HN and K60 Ha and between S61 HN and T54 Ha with equalized intensities indicating conformational averaging; weaker sequential HN-HN NOEs for 138-140 than 141-146; also cites published H/D exchange showing lack of protection at 53-61 and 138-141 vs protection at 142-149
residues_author: K51, L52, V53, T54, L55, N56, K58, L59, K60, S61 (lower lip strands beta3 V53-N56 and beta4 L59-S61); G129, F135, E136, H137, K138, A139, 140, S141 (upper lip and helix alpha6 N-terminus)
alt_state_structure: 1AM7: open form (molecules A and C) and closed form (molecule B) in apo X-ray crystal structure (Introduction, p. 1780; Fig. 1); 3D3D: closed form in complex with hexa-N-acetylchitohexaose (Introduction, p. 1780; Results and Discussion, p. 1785)
author_claim: Chemical shifts, 3JHNHa couplings, and interstrand/sequential NOEs show that open-like beta-strands beta3 and beta4 in the lower lip and helical turns at residues 136-139 of helix alpha6 in the upper lip are populated in solution but undergo substantial conformational averaging.
anchor: The 3JHNHa coupling constants measured for residues in this region (His137 6.1 Hz, Lys138 5.4 Hz, Ser141 5.9 Hz) are also consistent with fluctuating helical secondary structure.
locator: Results and Discussion, Chemical shift, coupling constant and NOE data for the lip regions, p. 1782-1783 and Fig. 3-4; Experimental Section, p. 1787
caveat_note: The 3JHNHa coupling constants were deposited in BMRB 19127 (p. 1787), while backbone chemical shifts and the 3D 15N-edited NOESY-HSQC came from ref. 9 and H/D exchange from ref. 12; the coupling/NOE Experimental Section paragraph does not explicitly restate sample temperature, pH, or solvent composition.

title: The dynamics of lysozyme from bacteriophage lambda in solution probed by NMR and MD simulations.
experiment: 10 ns explicit-solvent MD simulation (GROMOS 45A3 force field) starting from 1AM7 molecule A (open form)
buffer: SPC water (5063 water molecules, truncated octahedral box)
construct_or_mutation: wild-type bacteriophage lambda lysozyme sequence (aza-Trp in 1AM7 converted to Trp)
other_conditions: 1 atm constant pressure, 2 fs time step, 0.1 ps output, Asp/Glu unprotonated and 3 His singly protonated, preceded by 2 ps at 100 K and 2 ps at 200 K position-restrained equilibration; backbone N RMSF > 0.15 nm for residues 1-3, 22-28, 53-61, and 129-138; N-terminal region of helix alpha6 (135-139) unwinds within the first 1 ns but retains fluctuating helical turns; K58 Ca - E19 Ca distance spans 0.82 to 2.29 nm across the simulations
population: 53 NH...61 CO H-bond = 45.1 %; 61 NH...53 CO H-bond = 47.8 %; 59 NH...56 CO H-bond = 10.3 %; 138 NH...134 CO H-bond = 58.6 %; 138 NH...135 CO H-bond = 15.2 % (abstract summary: 40-60 %)
alt_state_structure: 1AM7: open form (molecules A and C) and closed form (molecule B) in apo X-ray crystal structure (Introduction, p. 1780; Fig. 1); 3D3D: closed form in complex with hexa-N-acetylchitohexaose (Introduction, p. 1780; Results and Discussion, p. 1785)
author_claim: MD simulation starting from the open conformation (1AM7 molecule A) shows elevated backbone fluctuations in the lower (53-61) and upper (129-138) lips, with fluctuating beta-sheet hydrogen bonds in the lower lip and transient helical-turn hydrogen bonds at residues 135-139.
locator: Results and Discussion, Molecular dynamics simulations, p. 1784-1786 and Fig. 6-8; conditions: Experimental Section, Molecular dynamics simulations, p. 1787-1788
caveat_note: Computational MD trajectory at 300 K rather than the 293 K experimental NMR sample; authors note the 10 ns simulation window is relatively short compared with slower microsecond-millisecond motions inferred from NMR Rex.

other_conditions: 1AM7 asymmetric unit contains molecules A and C in open form (beta3 V53-N56 and beta4 L59-S61 present; helix alpha6 starts at F135) and molecule B in closed form (beta3/beta4 absent as long loop; first turn of helix alpha6 unwound so helix starts at A139); PISA shows intermolecular H-bonds between P57 and K58 of molecule B and N6 of molecule C in 1AM7
